entities.evidence: Genesis 10:2 names Gomer as a son of Japheth. This verse names Gomer’s three sons.
Ashkenaz is the first person listed among Gomer’s sons.
Riphath is named between Ashkenaz and Togarmah in the list of Gomer’s sons.
Togarmah is the third person listed among Gomer’s sons.

draft.change: Add Genesis 10:3 as evidence for the existing ben-son sense of בֵּן in the ben article.
draft.definition: A male child in relation to his parent.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:3 places גֹּמֶר after the plural construct בְנֵי and then names his three sons.

analysis.evidence: וּבְנֵי גֹּמֶר introduces Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah by name as Gomer’s sons.
analysis.morphology: וּ is the prefixed conjunction “and.” בְנֵי is the masculine plural construct of the common noun בֵּן. The following name גֹּמֶר completes the construct phrase.

analysis.evidence: וּבְנֵי גֹּמֶר introduces Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah as Gomer’s sons. This genealogical construction identifies גֹּמֶר as the personal name.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix, governed by the construct plural בְנֵי.

draft.change: Add a Hebrew personal-name article for Ashkenaz. The name’s Hebrew derivation is unknown.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:3 names Ashkenaz first among Gomer’s sons.

analysis.evidence: The phrase וּבְנֵי גֹּמֶר means “and the sons of Gomer.” אַשְׁכֲּנַז is the first name in that list, followed by וְרִיפַת and וְתֹגַרְמָה.
analysis.morphology: A masculine personal name, singular and unprefixed, with no suffix. Its first כ bears a ḥaṭef pataḥ in this verse.
analysis.sense: The son of Gomer listed alongside Riphath and Togarmah.

draft.change: Add a Hebrew personal-name article for רִיפַת with the root unassigned. The genealogy gives no support for דינ or the gloss “regard; recognize.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:3 lists Riphath second among Gomer’s sons.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 10:3, וּבְנֵי גֹּמֶר (“and the sons of Gomer”) introduces three names. רִיפַת comes between Ashkenaz and Togarmah. The list identifies the bearer but gives no etymology.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and” and joins the personal name רִיפַת to the list of Gomer’s sons.

draft.change: Add a Hebrew personal-name article for Togarmah. The genealogy supports the name and its bearer. It supplies no basis for the source root תבנ or the gloss “ships; fleet.”
draft.definition: Togarmah, a son of Gomer named in Genesis 10:3.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 10:3, Togarmah is the final name in the list headed by וּבְנֵי גֹּמֶר, “and the sons of Gomer.”

analysis.evidence: וּבְנֵי גֹּמֶר introduces the sons of Gomer. וְתֹגַרְמָה names the third son listed, after Ashkenaz and Riphath. The verse identifies the bearer but gives no etymology for his name.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and” and joins the proper name תֹגַרְמָה to the preceding names.
